Class ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier1.ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Dynamic Thermohaline Circulation & Stommel (1961) 2-Box Overturning Engine.

Models the non-linear dynamics, hysteresis, and bistability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) across deep-time timescales (from $-3\,000\,000$ BP to $+100\,000$ CE) based on the canonical two-box formulation of Henry Stommel (1961):

Stommel 2-Box Coupled Differential Equations: $$\frac{dT_p}{dt} = \frac{T_p^* - T_p}{\tau_T} + |q| \frac{T_e - T_p}{V_p}$$ $$\frac{dS_p}{dt} = \frac{S_p^* - S_p}{\tau_S} + |q| \frac{S_e - S_p}{V_p} - \frac{F_{\text{melt}}}{V_p}$$

where:

  • $T_p, S_p$: Subpolar North Atlantic polar box temperature (Â°C) and salinity (PSU).
  • $T_e, S_e$: Equatorial / Tropical Atlantic box temperature ($28.0^\circ\text{C}$) and salinity ($36.5\text{ PSU}$).
  • $\tau_T \approx 20\text{ years}$: Fast atmospheric thermal relaxation timescale.
  • $\tau_S \approx 300\text{ years}$: Slow haline diffusion timescale providing multi-centennial memory.
  • $q$: Volume overturning flux in Sverdrups ($10^6\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$), $q = C (\alpha \Delta T - \beta \Delta S)$.
  • $F_{\text{melt}}$: Freshwater meltwater discharge flux (Sv), driven by Milankovitch orbital insolation at 65Â°N and greenhouse anomalies.

Bipolar Seesaw Response (Broecker 1998, EPICA 2006): An AMOC collapse deprives the North Atlantic and Western Europe of northward heat transport ($\Delta T_{\text{North}} \approx -8.0^\circ\text{C}$), while heat accumulation in the Southern Ocean triggers a compensatory warming ($\Delta T_{\text{South}} \approx +1.5\text{ to }+2.0^\circ\text{C}$).

    • stepStommelDynamics

      public static ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine.StommelState stepStommelDynamics(double freshwaterMeltwaterAnomalySv, double dtYears)
      Advances the Stommel 2-box differential equations over time $\Delta t$ with freshwater forcing $F_{\text{melt}}$. Uses internal numerical sub-cycling (dt invalid input: '<'= 1.0 year) to ensure unconditional numerical stability across deep time.
      Parameters:
      freshwaterMeltwaterAnomalySv - Freshwater meltwater anomaly (Sv)
      dtYears - Integration timestep in years
      Returns:
      current thermodynamic StommelState
